## RED evidence (current HEAD, `ium-core/tests/supervisor.rs::drive_is_callable_off_the_runtime_thread`)

The new test reproduces the shell's exact threading situation — a supervisor built inside a runtime, then `drive()` called from a thread where **no tokio context is entered** (the GTK main thread's permanent state during sync commands):

```
running 1 test
test drive_is_callable_off_the_runtime_thread ... FAILED

---- drive_is_callable_off_the_runtime_thread stdout ----

thread 'drive_is_callable_off_the_runtime_thread' (23259) panicked at ium-core/src/supervisor.rs:77:22:
there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace

failures:
    drive_is_callable_off_the_runtime_thread

test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 4 filtered out
```

`supervisor.rs:77` is the raw `tokio::spawn` inside `Supervisor::drive`. In the shell, this panic fires on the GTK main thread inside the webview IPC handler; the unwind crosses the FFI boundary, Rust aborts the process ("thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting." — captured in driver.log on CI #70), and WebKitWebDriver reports `Session terminated without a reply` — the exact failure of runs #65–#70.

Why every other test was green: they all construct and drive the supervisor inside `#[tokio::test]`, where the ambient context exists. The shell does not have that luxury.

**Why RED:** the contract under repair — drive() must be callable from any thread (tauri sync commands run on the main thread) — is violated at HEAD: the call panics instead of spawning.
